newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-MONACO CONFIDENT OF OVERHAULING PSG.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MONACO CONFIDENT OF OVERHAULING PSG.

text.p: Monaco, riding high on the domestic and European fronts, are looking forward to a tight race for the French first division championship with Paris Saint-Germain.
Now only one point behind the leaders, they hope to take over from PSG at the top for at least 24 hours with victory at Montpellier on Thursday.
PSG are away to Caen, like Montpellier candidates for relegation, on Friday.

In the slightly longer term and after the trip to Hamburg on Tuesday for a UEFA Cup third round tie they lead 3-0 after the first leg, Monaco aim to keep abreast of PSG until the winter break starting on December 20.
Then they entertain PSG in a crucial home clash when the season resumes on January 25.
Monaco are revelling in what they see as a psychological advantage over PSG.
"Can you imagine it if we move in front between now and then," enthused Brazilian striker Anderson.
"Our objective was to win something this season," he said of a team whose brilliant second half of the previous campaign was not quite good enough to make up for a poor start.
"It's Paris who are under the greater pressure...we are extremely confident.
"Montpellier can be a crucial match because it could make our lives easier afterwards if we win," said Anderson, adding the motivation was enormous being so close to the leaders.

"Paris know that we're right behind them and our strength, I believe, is that in the squad there aren't too many questions about Paris. We're thinking more about ourselves," midfielder Sylvain Legwinski said.
Coach Jean Tigana said: "We know Montpellier are in trouble but our objective is to win there and reach the break with a minimum gap behind PSG, or be in front."
Monaco's next two league games against Guingamp and Cannes are at home before a trip to Lens on December 20.
At Montpellier, Monaco will be without suspended playmaker Ali Benarbia and defender Patrick Blondeau, apart from the still convalescing Enzo Scifo and Emmanuel Petit.
"Ali is the best player in the team, he is of capital importance in our attacking movements," said Legwinski.
France's other UEFA Cup contenders Metz have a far tougher away assignment on Thursday. They face Jean-Pierre Papin's Bordeaux who inflicted a 5-3 defeat on PSG 11 days ago.
Bordeaux are on song up front with 11 goals in three games.
"We're in the middle of a boom at the moment," said playmaker Ibrahima Ba who has attracted the attention of Barcelona.
"We must negotiate this match carefully so we can prepare our next trip to (champions) Auxerre in calm."
Coach Rolland Courbis is concerned by a defence, the team's strong point early in the season, that has condeded eight goals in the last three games.
"There's been some carelessness," he said.
